mission_05: Excellent! You have implemented multiple quantum feature maps that encode classical data into quantum states with different trade-offs. Angle encoding is simple and hardware-efficient but uses one qubit per feature. Amplitude encoding is exponentially compact (log(n) qubits for n features) but requires complex state preparation. IQP encoding creates highly expressive feature spaces through Hadamard superposition, data-dependent phase rotations, and entangling interactions. The feature space analysis reveals how well the encoding separates data: low mean overlap and high effective dimension indicate a rich, expressive feature map. Choosing the right encoding is critical for quantum ML: it determines the inductive bias of the quantum model and whether the quantum feature space provides an advantage over classical alternatives.
